notes: California localization of the civic-leadership legacy model — the original edition: the Willie L. Brown Jr. Institute Track's home state (app iterations v28-v30). DISCLAIMER, carried from the app: this track is a proposal built from the Willie L. Brown Jr. Institute of Politics and Public Service's public mission and the Fellowship Program at San Francisco State University. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or reviewed by the Institute, SF State, or Mayor Brown. A named track would be offered under a partnership agreement and the Institute's review of every course. 5 tracks x 10 themes x 5 grade bands = 250 blocks. Expanded by tools/generate_pack.py.

tracks.name: The Fellowship ladder: service as a career

themes.theme: Service as a craft, not a slogan
themes.description: The founding principle taught as practice: public service with roles, crews, evidence and credentials, every course ending before a real audience.
themes.transfer_check: Complete one documented act of public service in your city or county and present it to a real audience beyond your classroom.

bands.K–2: Help someone with a real task and do it carefully, with an adult.
bands.3–5: Do a helping task carefully rather than just for show, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Perform a real act of service with genuine care and skill, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Approach real public service as a craft to be practiced, on your own.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else why real service is a craft, not a slogan.

themes.theme: The public servants of your city
themes.description: Mapping who serves within reach — the librarian, the transit operator, the caseworker, the inspector — and what each actually does all day.
themes.transfer_check: Interview one working public servant about a typical day and present their real duties against what you had assumed.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult who works for your city government.
bands.3–5: Name a real public servant in your city, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Identify several real public servants and their roles, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Research the real public servants who run key city functions, on your own.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else the real range of roles that keep a city running.

themes.theme: Who is missing from the room
themes.description: Inclusion as a design decision: reading any civic room for who is absent and naming the barrier that kept them out.
themes.transfer_check: Observe one real public meeting and report who was present, who was affected but absent, and one barrier that plausibly explains the gap.

bands.K–2: Notice who isn't included in a group activity, with an adult.
bands.3–5: Notice who's missing from a real decision-making group, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Identify who is real missing from a real decision-making room, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Identify and address who is missing from a real real room, on your own.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else why noticing who's missing from the room matters.

themes.theme: The placement inside a real agency
themes.description: The Fellowship pattern at every age — shadow days, junior placements and supervised hours inside city halls, libraries and public programs.
themes.transfer_check: Complete a placement, shadow day or structured volunteer shift with a real public body, confirmed by a supervisor.

bands.K–2: Visit a real government office with an adult and ask what happens there.
bands.3–5: Learn about a real government agency by visiting, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Complete a real short placement inside a real agency, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Complete a real substantive placement inside a real agency, on your own.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else what a real agency placement actually teaches.

themes.description: The weekly cohort habit the Fellowship runs on — field experience brought back to a circle that questions it.
themes.transfer_check: Run or take a speaking role in a seminar circle on a live local issue, presenting field evidence and taking questions.

bands.K–2: Sit in a circle and share an idea with classmates, with an adult.
bands.3–5: Discuss a real topic in a small group, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Participate in a real seminar-style discussion, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Lead a real seminar-style discussion on a real topic, on your own.
bands.11–12: Facilitate a real seminar circle that draws out quieter voices.

themes.description: The legacy chain: being mentored by someone ahead and mentoring someone behind, with the leader's-story interview as a core text.
themes.transfer_check: Record a leader's-story interview with an experienced public servant, and lead one session passing a skill to a younger learner.

bands.K–2: Help a younger student and learn from an older one, with an adult.
bands.3–5: Both give and receive help from others, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Practice real mentorship in both directions with a checker.
bands.9–10: Practice real two-way mentorship, giving and receiving, on your own.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else why real mentorship flows in both directions.

themes.description: First-generation pathways and the blocked door as history, law and practice — from segregated Mineola to the Speaker's chair, debate included.
themes.transfer_check: Research one Californian who broke a civic ceiling, and identify one barrier data shows still standing in your county, with the numbers.

bands.K–2: Try something a little hard and keep going, with an adult.
bands.3–5: Push past a real challenge in a group activity, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Identify a real barrier and push past it, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Push past a real limiting barrier in your own civic life, on your own.
bands.11–12: Help someone else push past a real ceiling they've hit.

themes.description: Why unpaid service filters who serves — stipends, scheduling and the economics of showing up, treated as program design.
themes.transfer_check: Cost out four weeks of a real volunteer or placement role and propose the support that would let a working student hold it.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult why some helping jobs pay and some don't.
bands.3–5: Learn that some public service roles come with pay, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Identify a real paid public service opportunity, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Evaluate a real stipended service opportunity, on your own.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else the real trade-offs of paid versus unpaid service.

themes.description: The service ledger — hours, artifacts, references, credentials — as a portfolio that opens doors.
themes.transfer_check: Assemble your own service ledger to date in a form a scholarship or employer could verify.

bands.K–2: Keep a small folder of things you're proud of, with an adult.
bands.3–5: Keep a simple record of things you've done, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Build a real record of your own real activities and growth, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Build a real substantive record of your own leadership work, on your own.
bands.11–12: Advise someone else on building a real record that reflects their growth.

themes.theme: The on-ramp: from classroom to Fellowship
themes.description: The grade-12 pathway toward public-affairs study and programs like the SF State Fellowship — requirements, timing, and the first application.
themes.transfer_check: Map three real next-step routes into California public service — requirements, deadlines, first application step completed or drafted.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult what happens after finishing a school program.
bands.3–5: Learn about a real path from school to a real fellowship, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Identify a real on-ramp from classroom to a real fellowship, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Plan your own real on-ramp from classroom to a real fellowship, on your own.
bands.11–12: Guide someone else through a real on-ramp into public service.

tracks.name: The county and the city: government closest to the door

themes.description: California's local layers — county, city, special district, school district — and which one governs the block you live on.
themes.transfer_check: Produce the one-page profile of your own county and city — population, governing bodies, three services each actually runs — from official sources.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult what county and city you live in.
bands.3–5: Learn your own real county and city, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Explain what a county does versus a city, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Explain, using real examples, how counties and cities divide power.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else how California's real county and city structure works.

themes.description: The county board of supervisors and the city council — what each decides, and finding the member whose district holds your address.
themes.transfer_check: Identify your actual supervisor and councilmember by district lookup and summarise one recent vote each has cast.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult who makes decisions for your town.
bands.3–5: Name a real local council member or supervisor, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Identify a real supervisor or council member's role, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Research a real supervisor or council member's actual work, on your own.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else what a real supervisor or council actually does.

themes.theme: The general plan and the zoning map
themes.description: How California cities decide what gets built — the general plan, zoning, and the housing-element fights that fill every chamber.
themes.transfer_check: Find your parcel's zoning on the real map and explain what could and could not lawfully be built there.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult why some areas have houses and some have stores.
bands.3–5: Learn that towns plan where things can be built, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Read a real zoning map for a real area, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Read and interpret a real general plan or zoning map, on your own.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else how a real general plan shapes a real community.

themes.theme: The school board and the schoolhouse
themes.description: School districts as the education government — boards, superintendents, budgets, and the meeting where your school's fate is set.
themes.transfer_check: Attend or watch one real school board meeting and report one decision, who voted how, and who it affects.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult who decides things about your school.
bands.3–5: Learn what a real school board does, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Identify a real decision a school board makes, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Attend or research a real school board meeting, on your own.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else how a real school board's decisions reach the schoolhouse.

themes.theme: Special districts and the water under everything
themes.description: Water, transit, fire and utility districts — the boards that tax and decide, largely unwatched, in the state where water is politics.
themes.transfer_check: Identify three special districts covering your own address, and for one find its board, budget and next public meeting.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult where the water for your town comes from.
bands.3–5: Learn that a special district manages real local water, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Identify a real special district and what it manages, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Research a real special district's role in your area, on your own.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else how real special districts operate underneath everything.

themes.theme: The county budget, followed to the sidewalk
themes.description: Where county and city money comes from — property tax under Proposition 13, sales tax, fees — and following one line to a visible outcome.
themes.transfer_check: From your county's actual budget, trace one revenue source to one service and check that service's condition where you live.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult who pays to fix a broken sidewalk.
bands.3–5: Learn that county money pays for real local repairs, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Trace a real county budget line to a real local service, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Trace a real county budget item to its real local effect, on your own.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else how to trace a real budget line to the sidewalk.

themes.theme: The permit, the complaint, the record
themes.description: The resident's three transactions — asking permission, reporting a problem, requesting a record under the Public Records Act — done correctly.
themes.transfer_check: Complete one real local-government transaction (permit lookup, 311 request, or public-records request) and document the outcome.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult what a permit is for and why it matters.
bands.3–5: Learn that building something needs a real permit, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Identify a real permit, complaint or record process, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Navigate a real permit, complaint, or record request process, on your own.
bands.11–12: Guide someone else through a real permit or complaint process.

themes.description: The Brown Act's open meetings, the speaker card, the two minutes — putting a comment on the record so it moves someone.
themes.transfer_check: Deliver (or fully rehearse to the real rules) a public comment to a local body on a live agenda item, structured for the record.

bands.K–2: Practice sharing your opinion clearly, with an adult.
bands.3–5: Share an opinion at a real meeting or with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Give a real effective public comment at a real meeting, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Give a real effective public comment that actually gets heard, on your own.
bands.11–12: Coach someone else on giving real public comment that lands.

themes.theme: City and county: who does what
themes.description: The services that switch at the city limit — and the consolidated exception of San Francisco, city and county in one.
themes.transfer_check: For your own address, produce the who-fixes-what card: five common problems each matched to the correct government and office.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult if the city or the county fixes the road.
bands.3–5: Learn the difference between city and county jobs, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Sort a real local service into city or county responsibility, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Explain, for a real issue, whether the city or county is responsible.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else how to tell whether an issue is a real city or county matter.

themes.description: Escalation above the local — grand juries, state oversight, the courts and the press — the accountability ladder.
themes.transfer_check: Take one real or case-study local failure and map its escalation ladder in order, drafting the first escalation document.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult what to do if a problem doesn't get fixed.
bands.3–5: Learn one step to take if local government doesn't help, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Identify a real escalation path when local government fails, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Escalate a real unresolved local government failure, on your own.
bands.11–12: Guide someone else through escalating a real local government failure.

tracks.name: Sacramento: the Legislature and the law

themes.theme: The capitol and the two chambers
themes.description: The Assembly and Senate, districts and leadership — including the Speaker's chair and what four decades there can build.
themes.transfer_check: Identify your actual Assembly member and state Senator by district lookup and summarise one bill each has authored recently.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult where laws for the state get made.
bands.3–5: Learn about the real state capitol building, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Identify the real two chambers of the state legislature, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Explain, using real roles, what each chamber of the legislature does.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else how the real two-chamber legislature actually functions.

themes.description: California's two-year session rhythm — introduction deadlines, house-of-origin deadlines, the August crush — and why timing decides outcomes.
themes.transfer_check: Find the current session's actual calendar and explain which deadlines a new idea introduced today would face.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult if lawmakers work all year.
bands.3–5: Learn that the legislature meets in a real session, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Identify a real deadline that shapes the legislative session, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Explain, using real deadlines, how the session shapes what passes.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else why real legislative deadlines matter so much.

themes.description: Filing, policy committee, appropriations, floor, the other house, the Governor's desk — following one real bill, including where bills die quietly.
themes.transfer_check: Track one real bill through each stage on the Legislature's own site and state where it stalled or how it became law.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult how an idea becomes a real rule.
bands.3–5: Learn the basic steps a real bill follows, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Trace a real bill's journey through the real legislature, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Trace a real bill's actual journey from idea to law, on your own.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else the real journey a bill takes, not the simplified version.

themes.theme: The committee room is the real floor
themes.description: Testimony, amendment and the suspense file — where bills actually live and die, and the citizen's seat at the microphone.
themes.transfer_check: Watch one real committee hearing (live or archived) and report the arguments, amendments and vote as the record shows.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult where the real decisions about a bill get made.
bands.3–5: Learn that committees do a lot of the real work, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Identify what real work happens in a real committee room, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Explain why the real committee room, not the floor, decides most bills.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else why the real committee room is where bills live or die.

themes.theme: The budget: the biggest bill of all
themes.description: The May Revise, the budget act and the trailer bills — how the state's money is actually decided and who watches it.
themes.transfer_check: From official budget documents, chart the state's five largest spending areas and follow one down to a program in your county.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult how the state decides what to spend money on.
bands.3–5: Learn that the state has a real big spending plan, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Identify a real major item in the state budget, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Trace a real state budget item to its real effect, on your own.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else why the real budget is the legislature's biggest bill.

themes.theme: Speaker, caucus and the art of counting
themes.description: How a chamber is actually run — leadership, caucuses and counting votes before the vote, the craft the Speaker's era made famous.
themes.transfer_check: For one real close vote, reconstruct the coalition: who moved, what they traded, and how the count was made.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult who leads a group of lawmakers.
bands.3–5: Learn what a real Speaker or caucus leader does, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Identify how a real Speaker counts votes within a caucus, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Explain, using real examples, how a real Speaker counts and holds votes.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else the real art of counting votes in a legislature.

themes.theme: The agencies that carry out the words
themes.description: Departments, boards and the administrative code — how a passed law becomes a rule, a form and an inspector.
themes.transfer_check: Pick one state rule that touches your life, find it in the code of regulations, and trace it to the statute that authorised it.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult who makes sure a rule actually happens.
bands.3–5: Learn that agencies carry out real laws, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Identify a real state agency that implements a real law, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Trace a real law to the real agency that carries it out, on your own.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else how real agencies turn a law's words into action.

themes.description: The routes from resident to lawmaking — contacting members, testifying, and the idea that becomes a filed bill.
themes.transfer_check: Draft a one-page bill proposal on a real local problem and deliver it (or rehearsed testimony for it) in proper form.

bands.K–2: Practice sharing your opinion clearly, with an adult.
bands.3–5: Share an opinion at a real hearing or with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Give real testimony on a real bill at a hearing, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Give real effective testimony on a real bill, on your own.
bands.11–12: Coach someone else on testifying effectively on a real citizen's bill.

themes.description: Superior courts, courts of appeal and the Supreme Court — how an ordinary case climbs, and how judges reach the bench.
themes.transfer_check: Map one real California case's path from filing to final ruling, naming each court correctly.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult what happens if people disagree about a law.
bands.3–5: Learn that real courts settle disagreements about laws, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Identify a real court above the county level and its role, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Explain, using a real case, how a real appeals court reviews a law.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else the real role of courts above the county level.

themes.theme: Working across the aisle and the decades
themes.description: Governing across administrations and parties — consensus that tolerates opposing ideas, taught from the record.
themes.transfer_check: Take one real bipartisan Californian achievement, identify what each side conceded and gained, and present the deal's anatomy.

bands.K–2: Work with someone who wants something different, with an adult.
bands.3–5: Cooperate with someone who disagrees with you, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Find real common ground across a real disagreement, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Build a real lasting agreement across the aisle, on your own.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else how real change happens across the aisle and decades.

tracks.name: Elections, initiatives and the direct voice

themes.description: Who may vote in California, same-day registration, and the habit of checking your own record.
themes.transfer_check: Verify a real registration (yours or a consenting adult's) through the state's official portal and correct any detail found wrong.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult how grown-ups sign up to vote.
bands.3–5: Learn what voter registration means, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Explain the real steps to register and stay registered, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Register or verify your own real registration status, on your own.
bands.11–12: Guide someone else through real voter registration and keeping it current.

themes.description: California's top-two system — every candidate on one ballot, two advance — and what it changes about strategy and choice.
themes.transfer_check: For two offices on a real ballot, explain the rules that currently govern each, citing the Secretary of State's guidance.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult how a first round of voting can narrow choices.
bands.3–5: Learn that some elections have two rounds, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Explain how a real top-two primary actually works, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Explain, using a real example, how the top-two primary shapes real races.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else how California's real top-two primary system works.

themes.theme: The initiative: writing law at the ballot box
themes.description: Direct democracy — initiative, referendum and recall — the signature thresholds, the money behind measures, and reading a proposition honestly.
themes.transfer_check: Take one real past or pending proposition, translate its ballot language into plain words, and present the strongest case each way with its funders named.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult if regular people can help make a rule.
bands.3–5: Learn that voters can create real laws directly, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Identify a real initiative and what it would change, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Evaluate a real ballot initiative's actual text and effect, on your own.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else how the real initiative process works, start to finish.

themes.description: Judges, school boards, special-district seats and local measures — the down-ballot lines that move your money and your block.
themes.transfer_check: Obtain your actual sample ballot for a real election and produce a plain-language guide for every line below the top race.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult about smaller choices on a ballot.
bands.3–5: Learn that ballots have many choices, not just the big ones, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Identify a real down-ballot race or measure, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Research a real down-ballot race or measure before voting, on your own.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else why the real ballot below the headlines matters.

themes.theme: Voting by mail, early and in person
themes.description: Universal mail ballots, drop boxes, vote centers and curing a rejected signature — the mechanics of actually being counted.
themes.transfer_check: Build the complete voting plan for two different real voters — one straightforward, one facing a barrier such as mobility, language or absence.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult about the different ways people vote.
bands.3–5: Learn the real different ways to cast a vote, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Explain the real options for voting by mail, early or in person, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Choose and use a real voting method that works for you, on your own.
bands.11–12: Guide someone else through choosing a real voting method.

themes.description: Poll workers, observers and the county elections office — the trained neighbours who run the machinery, and how to join them.
themes.transfer_check: Find your county's actual requirements and application to serve as an election worker and submit or fully prepare it.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult what a poll worker does on election day.
bands.3–5: Learn what a real poll worker's job involves, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Identify a real role someone could play working an election, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Volunteer or research a real role working a real election, on your own.
bands.11–12: Recruit someone else to work a real election in a real role.

themes.description: Campaign finance disclosure and the FPPC — following the money in one real race or measure through the public filings.
themes.transfer_check: Pull the actual campaign finance filings for one recent race or measure and report its top contributors and spending, with sources.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult why running for office costs so much money.
bands.3–5: Learn that campaign money must be reported, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Identify where real campaign finance information is disclosed, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Research real campaign finance disclosures for a real race, on your own.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else how real campaign money transparency works.

themes.description: Coalitions, petitions and the packed chamber — moving an issue between elections, counting votes before the vote.
themes.transfer_check: Organize or fully plan an issue campaign for one concrete local change: the decision-maker, the coalition map, the count you need.

bands.K–2: Ask a friend to help with something you care about, with an adult.
bands.3–5: Ask people to support a real cause, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Make a real organized ask for support on an issue, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Organise a real ask for support around a real issue, on your own.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else how to make a real effective organized ask.

themes.description: Election misinformation in California's channels — the claims that recur, and the official sources that settle them.
themes.transfer_check: Fact-check three circulating election claims against the Secretary of State and county officials' records and publish the corrected version.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult before believing something you heard about an election.
bands.3–5: Check a real election rumor before believing it, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Verify a real election-season rumor against real sources, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Verify real election rumors on your own before spreading them.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else how to handle real rumor season around an election.

themes.description: Canvass, the thirty-day certification, recounts and challenges — how results become final and what a citizen can lawfully question.
themes.transfer_check: Trace one real California race or measure from election night to certification, naming each step and any challenge lodged.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult what happens after votes are counted.
bands.3–5: Learn what happens after a real election ends, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Identify a real step that happens after a real vote count, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Explain, using a real example, what happens after a real count concludes.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else the real process that follows an election count.

tracks.name: Fire, water and the fault line

themes.theme: A state built on faults and watersheds
themes.description: California's geography as its permanent civic agenda — quake, fire, drought and flood, and the institutions each has built.
themes.transfer_check: Map the hazards that shape your own county — fault zones, fire severity zones, flood maps — from official sources.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult why the ground sometimes shakes.
bands.3–5: Learn that California has real faults and watersheds, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Identify a real fault or watershed near you, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Explain, using real geography, how faults and watersheds shape the state.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else how California's real geology shapes its risks.

themes.description: Wildfire as governance — defensible space law, red-flag warnings, utility shutoffs, and the evacuation decided before smoke.
themes.transfer_check: Assess a real or case-study property's wildfire exposure, specify its defensible-space actions, and write its trigger-based leave plan.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult why some years have more fires.
bands.3–5: Learn that fire season has gotten longer over time, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Identify a real cause behind a longer fire season, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Explain, using real evidence, why fire season has lengthened.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else the real evidence behind a longer fire season.

themes.description: Building codes, retrofits, early-warning systems and the drill — living on the fault line as civic practice.
themes.transfer_check: Run the full drop-cover-hold drill in two rooms, then complete the post-shake checklist — gas, structure, exits — in order.

bands.K–2: Practice an earthquake drill with an adult.
bands.3–5: Know one earthquake safety step, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Prepare for a real expected earthquake using a checklist, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Prepare yourself and a household for a real expected earthquake, on your own.
bands.11–12: Lead a real household's earthquake preparation and response plan.

themes.theme: Water: who gets it and who decides
themes.description: The projects, the rights, the districts and the drought rules — the century-long argument that runs the state.
themes.transfer_check: Trace your own tap water to its actual sources and name the two decision-making bodies with the most power over it.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult where the water for your town comes from.
bands.3–5: Learn that water rights are decided by real rules, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Identify a real water rights decision-maker, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Explain, using a real example, how water allocation decisions get made.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else the real politics behind who gets water.

themes.description: Public-safety power shutoffs, the duck curve and the batteries — keeping a household and a block running when the grid blinks.
themes.transfer_check: Prepare a real household for a planned outage — essentials, medical needs, neighbours checked — and run a two-hour drill.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult why the power sometimes gets turned off on purpose.
bands.3–5: Learn that power can be shut off to prevent fires, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Identify a real reason for a planned power shutoff, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Prepare for a real planned power shutoff, on your own.
bands.11–12: Advise a household on preparing for a real planned power shutoff.

themes.theme: Housing and the ground it stands on
themes.description: The housing shortage as civic machinery — RHNA numbers, the housing element, and the hearing where units are won or lost.
themes.transfer_check: Attend or watch one real housing hearing, and report the project, the arguments on each side and the outcome.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult why some houses are built differently in risky areas.
bands.3–5: Learn that homes are built to handle real local risks, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Identify a real building requirement for a real hazard zone, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Evaluate a real home's readiness for its real local hazard, on your own.
bands.11–12: Advise someone else on real building considerations for a hazard-prone area.

themes.theme: The coast and the king tide
themes.description: Sea-level rise on a 840-mile coast — the commissions, the managed-retreat argument, and the neighbourhoods already deciding.
themes.transfer_check: For one real coastal community, summarise its current adaptation plan and the hardest trade-off inside it.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult why the ocean sometimes comes up higher.
bands.3–5: Learn what a real king tide is, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Identify a real coastal risk from a real king tide, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Explain, using real data, how a real king tide affects the coast.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else the real risk a king tide poses to coastal areas.

themes.description: CERT teams, community fire brigades and the block-level networks that carry the first seventy-two hours.
themes.transfer_check: Complete or map enrolment in one recognised local response group, and build the (consented) support map for one street.

bands.K–2: Help a neighbour with a small task, with an adult.
bands.3–5: Help a real neighbour during a hard time, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Organise a real mutual aid effort for neighbours, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Organise real mutual aid for your own neighbourhood, on your own.
bands.11–12: Lead a real neighbourhood mutual aid system during an emergency.

themes.description: After the fire or quake — insurance, the FAIR plan, rebuilding permits, and why the same event lands unequally.
themes.transfer_check: From one documented California disaster, chart the recovery programs and identify, with evidence, one group the paperwork left behind.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult what happens to a home after a disaster.
bands.3–5: Learn that some homes get rebuilt faster than others, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Identify a real inequity in a real disaster recovery process, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Advocate for a real fair recovery process after a real disaster, on your own.
bands.11–12: Advocate for a real vulnerable group's fair treatment in real disaster recovery.

themes.description: The capstone: civic leadership where fire, water and ground are all in motion — weighing protection, retreat and cost with real neighbours in the room.
themes.transfer_check: Run or present a structured deliberation on one real local resilience decision — options, trade-offs, affected voices — and deliver the recommendation you would defend in public.

bands.K–2: Stay calm and help others during a scary time, with an adult.
bands.3–5: Help keep others calm during a real ongoing emergency, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Lead a real small group through a real ongoing emergency, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Lead others through a real long emergency, on your own.
bands.11–12: Guide a real community through a real long, ongoing emergency.
